title: Integration orientation of the actual normal-section invariant
statement: Fix a finite purity setting P, its coefficient ring A and exponent m as in [def-pur-conventions], and a normalized etale compact-support datum N. Let B be a finite-type k-scheme, aB its structure map, and let g:V->B be smooth separated of pure dimension d, quasi-compact, with a closed section s and g s=1 [def-pur-section-restriction-data]. Let F=I_s/I_s^2 be its rank-d conormal module [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-interfaces]. Define normalIntegration:C_A(pi_N,z)~A_B(d)[2d], where pi_N is the actual normal projection, as follows. Use the homogeneous Rees comparison and the symmetric conormal comparison to identify the actual normal cone with the vector bundle Spec Sym F, preserving projection and zero. Apply the etale section restriction along the inverse model isomorphism [def-pur-diagonal-dnc-chart-data], followed by bundleOrientation, the inverse of the actual zero-section integration adjunct [def-pur-bundle-integration-orientation]. Apply the etale/pro-etale comparison pullback and precompose the canonical normalComparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. This is exactly the existing normalIntegration construction, relocated without a changed signature or body.

proof.text: The homogeneous Rees comparison followed by coneBundleIso is an isomorphism e from the actual normal cone to Spec Sym F. Their projection and augmentation equations give e pi_F=pi_N and z e=z_F. Invert e and use the two inverse equations to obtain the projection and section equations for e inverse.

Compose the specified etale-locality section isomorphism for e inverse with bundleOrientation, apply the comparison-site functor, and precompose normalComparison. All terms are actual constructions; no object is chosen from mere existence.
